item.title: Pope Leo decries world 'ravaged by tyrants' amid feud with Trump
item.description: Pope Leo XIV delivered some of his most forceful remarks yet on Thursday, declaring that the world is "being ravaged by a handful of tyrants" during a peace gathering in the conflict-scarred city of Bamenda, Cameroon. The address, made at Saint Joseph Cathedral on the second day of his Cameroon visit, came amid an escalating public feud with U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the pontiff's opposition to the war in Iran.

item.title: White House clears path for federal agencies to use Anthropic's Mythos AI
item.description:
The White House Office of Management and Budget is establishing security protocols to allow major federal agencies to begin using Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, the powerful AI model that has rattled cybersecurity experts and financial regulators on both sides of the Atlantic since its limited release earlier this month. Federal CIO Gregory Barbaccia informed Cabinet departments of the plan, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg.

The move comes even as government officials grapple with the model's potential to sharply increase cybersecurity risk — and despite an ongoing legal and political clash between the Trump administration and Anthropic over the use of the company's AI technology.

item.title: Trump says Iran agreed to hand over enriched uranium as deal nears
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Thursday that Iran has agreed to relinquish its stockpile of enriched uranium, claiming the two sides are "close" to a peace deal to end over six weeks of war. The assertion came as Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian negotiators have scaled back ambitions for a comprehensive agreement and are instead pursuing a temporary memorandum to prevent a return to hostilities before the ceasefire expires on April 21.

A separate source told Reuters that Iran had agreed to dilute its highly enriched uranium under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the United States. A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of parliament, said earlier this week that Tehran had agreed to dilute 450 kilograms of enriched uranium as a goodwill measure, though he added that the United States later backed out of that arrangement.

item.title: IMF says Asia faces worst exposure to Middle East energy shock
item.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Thursday that Asia is more exposed than any other region to the energy shock unleashed by the war in the Middle East, as the fund's spring meetings in Washington laid bare the widening economic toll of the conflict on the world's poorest nations.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire set to take effect at 5 p.m. EST, pausing weeks of devastating Israeli strikes against Hezbollah that have killed more than 2,000 people in Lebanon since early March.

"These two Leaders have agreed that in order to achieve PEACE between their Countries, they will formally begin a 10 Day CEASEFIRE at 5 P.M. EST," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the agreement followed "excellent" conversations with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Trump said he would invite both leaders to the White House for what he called "the first meaningful talks between Israel and Lebanon since 1983." He also said he had directed Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to work with both countries toward "a Lasting PEACE."

item.title: China activates 60,000-chip AI science cluster built without US tech
item.description: China activated its largest artificial intelligence computing cluster for scientific research on Tuesday in Zhengzhou, central Henan province, doubling the facility's chip count from 30,000 to 60,000 domestically produced AI accelerators in just two months. The expansion, carried out entirely without American technology, marks a milestone in Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency in advanced computing amid tightening U.S. export controls.

item.title: Lebanon death toll reaches 2,196 as Israeli strikes continue
item.description:
Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health confirmed on Thursday that the cumulative death toll from Israeli military operations has risen to 2,196, with 7,185 others wounded since the conflict with Hezbollah erupted on March 2, according to the ministry's daily report from its Health Emergency Operations Center. In the past 24 hours alone, at least 29 people were killed and 124 wounded in strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon, Anadolu Agency reported.

The escalating toll prompted Imran Riza, the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator for Lebanon, to warn that the human cost has "crossed a devastating threshold," noting more than 2,000 killed and 1.2 million displaced.

item.title: NASA probe detects surprise solar explosion behavior
item.description: NASA announced Wednesday that its Parker Solar Probe detected a surprise explosion near the Sun, revealing that different particles are flung into space in unexpectedly different ways during the magnetic events that power solar storms.

item.title: Study outlines four options for saving Venice from rising seas
item.description:
A team of European researchers has laid out four possible futures for Venice — ranging from reinforcing its existing flood defenses to abandoning the city entirely — warning that without early action, the iconic UNESCO World Heritage Site could be lost within centuries.

The study, published Wednesday in the journal Scientific Reports, was led by oceanographer Piero Lionello of the University of Salento in Italy. It presents what the authors call an "adaptation pathways" framework, mapping out which strategies remain viable as sea levels climb under different emissions scenarios drawn from the IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report.

item.title: Sanctioned vessels breach US naval blockade of Iran
item.description: At least two sanctioned cargo vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz and reached Iranian waters on Thursday despite the U.S. Navy's blockade of Iranian ports, raising questions about the effectiveness of enforcement now entering its fourth day.

item.title: Israeli shelling hits south Lebanon minutes after ceasefire takes effect
item.description:
Less than an hour after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon officially went into effect on Thursday evening, fresh shelling struck towns in southern Lebanon, casting immediate doubt over the durability of the truce.

Lebanon's National News Agency reported that Israeli artillery continued to shell the towns of Khiam and Dibbine after the 5 p.m. ET (21:00 GMT) deadline passed, with sweeping operations involving machine-gun fire also reported in the area. The Israeli military simultaneously warned residents of southern Lebanon not to move south of the Litani River, stating that its forces remain deployed there.

item.title: Trump warns U.S. 'won't be there' for Italy over airbase denial
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his feud with Italy on Wednesday, posting on Truth Social that "Italy wasn't there for us, we won't be there for them!" — a sharp warning directed at one of Washington's closest European allies over Rome's refusal to allow U.S. military aircraft to use the Sigonella airbase in Sicily for operations linked to the ongoing war in Iran.

The post, which linked to a Guardian report on the incident, caps weeks of deteriorating relations between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, once considered Europe's most reliable bridge to the White House.

item.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire takes effect as gold rises on peace hopes
item.description: Gold prices rose on Thursday as the U.S. dollar weakened, with investors growing optimistic that diplomatic progress in the Middle East — including a newly announced ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon and the prospect of renewed U.S.-Iran negotiations — could ease the geopolitical pressures that have roiled markets for weeks.

item.title: Oil prices fall as Trump announces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire
item.description: Oil prices retreated on Thursday after President Donald Trump expressed optimism about the prospect of ending the war with Iran, even as the broader energy market remained on edge over continued disruptions in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Starmer and Macron host 40-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is set to arrive in Paris on Friday to co-host a summit with French President Emmanuel Macron aimed at restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway that carries roughly 20% of the world's oil supply. Around 40 countries are expected to join the virtual meeting, which Downing Street described as advancing "a coordinated, independent, multinational plan to safeguard international shipping once the conflict ends".

Starmer is expected to tell the gathering that "the unconditional and immediate reopening of the Strait is a global responsibility," urging international leaders to act collectively to get "global energy and trade flowing freely again". The initiative, formally called the Strait of Hormuz Maritime Freedom of Navigation Initiative, will focus on supporting the fragile ceasefire in the region and developing plans for mine clearance and military assurance for commercial shipping.

item.title: Iran war drives nuclear power surge across Asia and Africa
item.description:
The energy shock unleashed by the 2026 Iran war is pushing nations across Asia and Africa to ramp up nuclear power generation and accelerate long-dormant atomic energy plans, as countries scramble to insulate themselves from the worst oil and gas disruption in modern history.

The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz — the chokepoint for roughly 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas — has cut off fuel supplies that Asian economies in particular depend on, according to the Associated Press. African and Asian nations that already operate nuclear plants are boosting output for immediate relief, while countries without reactors are fast-tracking development programs that could take decades to bear fruit but may reshape energy policy for a generation.

item.title: Asian stocks near pre-war levels as oil drops on ceasefire hopes
item.description: Asian equities were on track for a second consecutive week of gains and oil prices held below $100 a barrel on Friday, as growing optimism over a potential extension of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire buoyed investor sentiment across global markets.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz sees more ships despite US blockade
item.description: The Iran war's closure of the Strait of Hormuz — described by the International Energy Agency as the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market" — is reshaping energy policy across Asia and Africa, driving nations toward nuclear power and alternative crude suppliers as fossil fuel flows from the Gulf remain choked nearly seven weeks after hostilities began.

item.title: Thousands of displaced Lebanese head south as ceasefire takes hold
item.description: Thousands of displaced Lebanese families surged onto highways heading south on Friday, hours after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect at midnight local time, halting weeks of devastating conflict that killed more than 2,100 people and uprooted over a million from their homes.

item.title: Trump says Iran deal is close as Lebanon ceasefire takes hold
item.description:
President Donald Trump expressed confidence on Thursday that a deal to end the war with Iran is within reach, as a new 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon went into effect and diplomatic channels intensified ahead of a critical deadline next week.

"I think we're very close to making a deal with Iran," Trump told reporters outside the White House on Thursday. Speaking later in Las Vegas, he went further, saying the war "should be ending pretty soon". Trump indicated that a second round of in-person talks between the United States and Iran could take place as soon as this weekend in Islamabad, Pakistan, and said he might travel there himself if an agreement is signed.
